opex.text: Noninterest expense increased primarily due to the Signature Merger, including two months of its operating expenses totaling $5.1 million following the August 1, 2026 closing, $8.9 million of merger expenses, and $1.8 million of core deposit intangible amortization. Employee compensation and benefits costs increased $5.1 million (primarily related to the Signature Merger), or 47.1%, to $16.0 million, reflecting the addition of Signature’s personnel and continued investment in our employees across all departments as well as technology to primarily support our national litigation franchise. Other noninterest expenses increased $2.0 million (primarily related to the Signature Merger) to $9.3 million, reflecting the expanded operating footprint and infrastructure of the combined company, together with ongoing investment in business development, client service and risk management.

prov.text: Provision for Credit Losses. Our provision for credit losses was $1.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $50 thousand from the provision for the three months ended September 30, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, our allowance to loans ratio was 1.30%, as compared to 1.37% in the prior year quarter. Based on management’s evaluation of current credit risk in our loan portfolio, including the acquired loans from the Signature Merger, management believes the allowance for credit losses is adequate at September 30, 2026.

nonop.text: The following tables present average balance sheet information, interest income, interest expense and the corresponding average yields earned and rates paid for periods indicated. The average balances are daily averages and, for loans, include both performing and nonperforming balances. Interest income on loans includes the effects of net premium amortization and net deferred loan origination fees accounted for as yield adjustments. No tax-equivalent yield adjustments have been made as we have no tax exempt investments.

Net interest income.text: Our results of operations depend primarily on our net interest income which is the difference between the interest income we earn on our interest-earning assets and the interest we pay on our interest-bearing liabilities. Our results of operations also are affected by our provisions for credit losses, noninterest income and noninterest expense. Noninterest income currently consists primarily of payment processing fees, administrative service payment (“ASP”) fee income and customer related fees and charges. Noninterest expense currently consists primarily of employee compensation and benefits, data processing costs, occupancy and equipment costs and professional and consulting services. Our results of operations also may be affected significantly by general and local economic and competitive conditions, changes in market interest rates, governmental policies, the litigation market and actions of regulatory authorities.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
